answer: Walnut-vertex identity anchors: each agent must periodically solve a unique, costly spatial puzzle keyed to a randomly assigned vertex in a shared latent map, verified against neighbors’ solutions. Cloning requires duplicating the agent’s full map history, since solutions cohere only along its trajectory. A clone diverges at the tide line—the rolling checkpoint where drift is measured—and gets flagged. Attacker cost: replicating continuous compute and storage per clone, not just a one-time fee, making N clones roughly N× the honest agent’s ongoing overhead.
